title: Affine higher direct images lower the transcendence-degree support bound
statement: Let $K$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be schemes of finite type over $K$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $f:X\to Y$ be an affine $K$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-over-base], [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. For each integer $b$, put $E_b(T)=\{t\in T:\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(t)\leq b\}$, with $E_b(T)=\varnothing$ for $b<0$, using [def-kun-support] and [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Let $a\geq0$ be an integer and $F$ a torsion abelian etale sheaf on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf] whose support is contained in $E_a(X)$. Then, for every $q\geq0$, the support of $R^qf_*F$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is contained in $E_{a-q}(Y)$.

proof.text: Fix $q\geq0$ and a geometric point $\bar y$ of $Y$ whose underlying point $y$ has $b=\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(y)>a-q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply [prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula] to identify $(R^qf_*F)_{\bar y}$ with $H^q(T,F_T)$, where $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y,\bar y}$, $T=X\times_Y S$, and $F_T$ is the inverse image of $F$. It suffices to prove this group zero for each such geometric point, by the definition [def-kun-support].

source.place: Tag 0F0X, lemma-interlude-I, stalk calculation using Tag 03Q9

proof.text: Apply [lem-kun-strict-local-algebraic-residue-models] at $\bar y$. Write $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $X_U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ (affineness by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]), and $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}C_i$ for its models over the separably closed field $L$, where $\operatorname{trdeg}_K L=b$. Set $T_i=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A C_i)$ with projection $p_i:T_i\to X$ and $F_i=p_i^{-1}F$. The algebra $B$ is generated over $A$ by any finite set of its $K$-algebra generators, so each $T_i$ is affine finite type over $L$. All transition maps are affine. The equality $\varinjlim_i(B\otimes_A C_i)=B\otimes_A(\varinjlim_i C_i)$ follows from the universal property of tensor product and colimit: a map from either side is a compatible family of pairs of maps from $B,C_i$ agreeing on $A$. Thus $T=\varprojlim_iT_i$, over $X$. This uses no closed embedding into affine space.

source.place: Tags 0F0U and 0F0X, compatible-etale-model approximation; applied directly to an affine morphism

proof.text: For a point $z\in T_i$ put $x=p_i(z)$, and let $v\in V_i$ and $u\in U$ be its other images. The model lemma gives $\kappa(v)/\kappa(u)$ algebraic. The fibre of $T_i\to X_U$ at $x$ is obtained from $V_i$ by extending scalars from $\kappa(u)$ to $\kappa(x)$; its residue fields over $v$ are residue fields of $\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(u)}\kappa(v)$. This tensor product is integral over $\kappa(x)$, since each element of the algebraic extension $\kappa(v)$ satisfies a monic polynomial and any finite collection lies in a finite field extension. Its prime quotients are algebraic fields. Hence $\kappa(z)/\kappa(x)$ is algebraic. By [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar], a nonzero stalk of $F_i$ maps to a nonzero stalk of $F$; thus such an $x$ has $\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(x)\leq a$. Also $F_i$ is torsion, by the same stalk formula and [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-sheaf-characterizations].

source.place: Tag 0F0X, lemma-interlude-I, residue-extension and support calculation (using compatible models)

proof.text: For a point $z$ in the support of $F_i$, apply [lem-kun-transcendence-degree-tower] first to $K\subseteq\kappa(x)\subseteq\kappa(z)$ and then to $K\subseteq L\subseteq\kappa(z)$. The algebraic extension in the previous step has transcendence degree zero, so $b+\operatorname{trdeg}_L\kappa(z)=\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(z)=\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(x)\leq a$. If $b>a$ no such $z$ exists. In that case all geometric stalks of $F_i$ vanish, and [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] applied to $0\to F_i$ gives $F_i=0$, so its cohomology is zero in every degree. If $b\leq a$, the displayed inequality gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_L\kappa(z)\leq a-b$. Apply [lem-kun-affine-support-vanishing] to the affine finite-type $L$-scheme $T_i$ and torsion sheaf $F_i$, with nonnegative bound $c=a-b$. It gives $H^q(T_i,F_i)=0$ whenever $q>a-b$, which is exactly the inequality $b>a-q$ fixed in step 1.

source.place: Tag 0F0X, lemma-interlude-I, vanishing via Tag 0F0W, including the negative support-bound case

proof.text: The sheaves $F_i$ have the canonical pullback transition isomorphisms since all are inverse images of $F$ along the compatible maps to $X$. On $T$ their pullbacks are all $F_T$, so their filtered colimit is $F_T$. All schemes $T_i$ are affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated; the index category is small and cofiltered, and transitions are affine by step 2. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cofiltered-etale-cohomology-continuity] to get $H^q(T,F_T)=\varinjlim_iH^q(T_i,F_i)=0$. Step 1 now gives $(R^qf_*F)_{\bar y}=0$ for every geometric point above every $y$ with $b>a-q$. By [def-kun-support] this is precisely the claimed support containment. This also covers $q=0$, $q>a$, and the empty scheme.
